newsitem.title: USA: US rig count up 32 to 913 in week.
newsitem.headline: US rig count up 32 to 913 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 913 as of May 9, up 32 from the prior week and 141 above the year-ago total of 772, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 37 to 769, while rigs working offshore dropped by four to 119.

The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by one to 25. Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which rose by nine, Louisiana and Wyoming, which both rose by five and California, which rose by two.
Gulf of Mexico dipped five to 113.
A total of 374 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up five from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 27 to 535, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
There were 97 rigs drilling directionally, 67 drilling horizontally and 649 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 32 to 207, versus 78 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
